text:
mike: quick brain dump: what if we bucket prefixes into short-lived cohorts (hash-bucket + occasional merge) and make eviction decisions at cohort-level to reduce rehydrate churn?
ana: sounds promising. main concerns: RA-write for pinned prefixes, tenant isolation, and lookup overhead.
devon: agree. keep common-path cheap: try direct prefix lookup first, then consult cohort-index on miss. tombstone remap for moves.
kari: and add intra-cohort LRU so we don't evict all members at once. also circuit-breaker if cohort path increases p99.
mike: rollout: offline sim -> 0.5% read-only canary -> active canary -> ramp with feature flag and auto-rollback. include metrics: cohort_hit, remap_bounce, cohort_evict_rate, cohort_gc_delay.
ana: test matrix: chaos rebalances, pinned-key RA-write invariant tests, and long-lease GC behavior.
devon: I'll baseline current miss amplification and p99 this week.
kari: i'll prototype a tiny in-memory cohort-index (robin-hood hash) and measure mem overhead.
mike: cool, i'll draft RFC with pseudocode and thresholds. thanks all. :thumbsup:
